title: Optimizam result
description: The outcome of solving a problem file. See docs/result-format.md. A reader should ignore fields it doesn't know: later versions add fields.

version.description: The result format's version, "major.minor": the writer's, whatever the result holds. This schema describes major version 1; optimizam writes "1.2".

sense.description: The problem's solve method. It says which way objective_bound bounds: from below for minimize, from above for maximize.

objective_bound.description: Optional, when the search stopped without proving its answer (not_proven_optimal, locally_optimal, timeout): the best proven bound on the optimal objective value (an upper bound when maximizing, a lower bound when minimizing).

gap.description: Optional, with a solution and an objective_bound: |objective - objective_bound| / max(1, |objective|), how far from optimal the solution could be.

stop_reason.description: Optional: why the search stopped before it finished. Absent when it ran to its end.

conflict.description: Optional, only with status infeasible: why. Constraints that can't hold together given the variables' bounds and types, and variables whose own bounds or domain leave them no value. Without --explain only causes that can be read off the model are reported.

constraints.description: Constraint names, instances of indexed constraints written like "capacity[north]"; a constraint without a name is called by its place in the problem's list, counting from 0: "constraints[3]".

variables.description: Variables with no value left, written like "x" or "x[north,3]". Each is a cause by itself.

minimal.description: True if every member is needed: without any one of them the rest can hold.

unbounded.description: Optional, only with status unbounded: the variables with an objective coefficient and no bound in the direction that improves the objective. One of them is usually missing a bound.

omitted.description: What was left out of the solutions on request: "zeros" (zero entries of indexed variables and reduced costs: a missing entry is 0) and "slack" (constraints with slack). Absent when nothing was.

engine.description: The engine the problem went to; "presolve" if it was settled before any ran.

threads.description: The threads its search could use.

time.description: Seconds from the start of the solve (after the problem file was read) to the result.

nodes.description: The size of the search: branch-and-bound nodes (milp), conflicts (cp), or boxes (global).

objective.description: Objective value of this solution. Present exactly when the problem's solve method is minimize or maximize.

variables.description: Every variable in the problem, by name. A scalar variable maps to its value; an indexed variable maps to a table nested one object level per index set, keyed by set element (integers written as strings), like parameter values. Values are numbers, or for symbolic set-valued variables elements of their set.

constraints.description: With --constraints: every comparison (expr) constraint by name, instances of indexed constraints written like "capacity[north]" and constraints without a name by their place ("constraints[3]").

slack.description: How far the constraint's left side is from its right side in this solution (from the nearer bound, if it has two); 0 when it is tight.

enforced.description: false, in place of slack, when the constraint's enforce_if doesn't hold in this solution.

dual.description: For a linear program: the change of the optimal objective per unit that the constraint's right side rises, in the problem's own sense.

reduced_costs.description: With --constraints, for a linear program: each variable's reduced cost, laid out like variables: the change of the optimal objective per unit that the variable is moved off the bound it sits at (0 for one between its bounds).

value.description: A number, or an element of a symbolic set-valued variable's set.
